deities: Lord Shiva as Madanantheshwara ('god who killed Kama, god of desires') - presiding deity; Udbhava (self-manifested) shiva lingam discovered by Madaru of the Tulu Moger community

Lord Ganesha as Siddhi Vinayaka / Bodda Ganesha - more popularly worshipped; image drawn by a priest's young son on the southern wall of the garbhagriha, which legend says grew ever larger; faces south within the same sanctum
Kashi Vishwanatha, Dharmasastha, Subrahmanya, Durga Parameshwari, Veerabhadra and Gulika (sub-deities)
festivals: Moodappa Seva - periodic covering of the ~2-metre Mahaganapathi with appam (huge expenditure; last noted April 1992 per one source - verify)

history.dynasty: Under the Kumbla Rajas (Maipady Palace) historically; now managed by the government/Devaswom Board
history.period: 10th century AD per velpu.com (single weakly-sourced claim - verify); legend of Tipu Sultan's abandoned attack dated 1784
history.summary: One of the six Ganapathi temples of ancient Tulunadu (with Sharavu Mahaganapathy Mangalore, Anegudde, Hattiangadi, Idagunji and Gokarna). Originally the Madhanentheswara Shiva temple: lore says an old woman called Madaru from the local Tulu Moger community discovered an 'Udbhava Murthy' (not made by human hands) shiva lingam. The Ganapathi image was drawn by a priest's young son on the garbhagriha's southern wall while playing; day by day it grew big and fat, so the boy called him 'Boddajja' (Bodda Ganesha). Shiva and Ganapathi are worshipped together in the same sanctum - father and son receiving simultaneous worship in one Garbhagriha. The Kumble-seme legend says Tipu Sultan intended to demolish the temple during his 1784 invasion, but after drinking water from the temple well he spared the Garbhagudi; to satisfy his soldiers he made a cut with his sword, whose mark is still shown on the building around the well. The 3-tiered gajaprishta (elephant-back) sreekovil has copper roofing and exquisite wooden carvings of Ramayana scenes. Priests belong to the Shivalli Brahmin community; the temple runs summer Veda classes for young vatus. CSV TOWN FLAG: the temple is NOT in Kasaragod town - it is at Madhur village, on the banks of the Mogral (Madhuvahini) river, about 7 km from Kasaragod. Documented with the corrected location.

name: Madhur Temple
town: Madhur (CSV town 'Kasaragod' is the district HQ ~7 km away - corrected)
town_description: Madhur is a village about 7 km from Kasaragod district headquarters, on the banks of the Mogral river (locally Madhuvahini). The temple rises majestically against the river's landscape on Madhur Temple Road.

travel.road: 7 km from Kasaragod town on Madhur Temple Road; private buses run about every 10 minutes (7 AM - 8 PM); autos available.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; avoid the monsoon - the adjoining river can overflow onto the temple campus (per Wikipedia).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Official (madhurtemple.in): 5:00 AM - 1:00 PM and 5:30 PM - 8:15 PM daily. Note: entry restricted to Hindus; traditional attire advised.
